items.prompt_en: Listen: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Which word fits: 'true' or 'tight'?
items.prompt_hi: Suno: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Kaunsa word fit hoga, 'true' ya 'tight'? Rhyme ka dhyaan rakho.
items.answer: true
hints: Say the last word of the first line again.
The missing word must rhyme with 'two'.
It is 'true'. Two and true rhyme.

items.prompt_en: 'two' and 'true' are spelt differently at the end. Say them aloud. Do they rhyme?
items.prompt_hi: 'two' aur 'true' ki spelling alag hai. Dono ko zor se bolo. Kya rhyme karte hain?
items.answer: yes
hints: Close your eyes and just listen.
Rhyme is about sound, not letters.
Both end with the sound 'oo'. So do they rhyme?
Yes. Two and true rhyme even though they are spelt differently.

items.prompt_en: In our poem, what do many raindrops make?
items.prompt_hi: Hamari poem mein bahut saari boondein milkar kya banati hain?
items.answer: a waterfall
hints: Think of the line about one raindrop.
One raindrop is very small, but many drops make a ...
It rhymes with 'small': water-___.
Many drops make a waterfall.

items.prompt_en: Why does a bundle of ten sticks not snap, when one stick snaps easily?
items.prompt_hi: Ek stick aasani se toot jaati hai, par das sticks ka bundle kyun nahi toot-ta?
items.answer: Because many sticks together are stronger than one stick alone
hints: What is different between one stick and ten sticks?
Think about how strong each one is.
Together, the sticks are ... than one?
Ten sticks together are much stronger than one stick alone.

items.prompt_en: Riya cannot lift a heavy box of books alone. Three friends come to help her. What will happen next?
items.prompt_hi: Riya akele books ka bhaari box nahi utha paati. Uske teen dost help karne aate hain. Ab aage kya hoga?
items.answer: They will lift the box together
acceptable: they will carry the box together
hints: Think about the bundle of sticks.
What can four children do that one cannot?
Together they can ... the box?
They will lift the box together, just like the bundle of sticks is strong.

items.prompt_en: Your little brother asks, 'What is this poem about?' Explain it to him in two short sentences.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota bhai poochhta hai, 'Ye poem kis baare mein hai?' Use do chhote sentences mein samjhao, English mein try karo.
items.answer: When people work together they become strong and can do hard things; one stick or one raindrop is weak, but many together are strong
acceptable: we can do big things together
hints: What happens to one stick, and to ten sticks?
Now think of people instead of sticks.
Say: 'Together we are ...'
The poem says that together we are strong and can do hard things, like a bundle of sticks.

items.prompt_en: Fill in the gap: 'A ___ of sticks is hard to break.' Is it 'bundle' or 'bubble'?
items.prompt_hi: Khaali jagah bharo: 'A ___ of sticks is hard to break.' 'bundle' ya 'bubble'?
items.answer: bundle
hints: Think of many sticks tied up together.
A bubble is made of soap and air.
Bundle. A bundle of sticks is hard to break.

items.prompt_en: What is the English word for 'saath milkar'?
items.prompt_hi: 'Saath milkar' ko English mein kya kehte hain? Poem ki aakhri line yaad karo.
items.answer: together
hints: Look at the last line of the poem.
It starts with 'to-'.
'___ we can open doors.'
Together. 'Saath milkar' is 'together'.

items.prompt_en: Make your own sentence with the word 'together'.
items.prompt_hi: 'together' word use karke apna khud ka ek sentence banao. Ghar ya school ki koi baat socho.
items.answer: Any correct sentence using 'together', for example: We clean our classroom together.
acceptable: My sister and I cook together.
We sing together in the assembly.
hints: Think of something you do with friends or family.
Who does it with you?
Try: 'My friends and I ___ together.'
For example: My friends and I play cricket together.

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 'Ten ants can carries a leaf.'
items.prompt_hi: Is sentence mein galti dhoondo: 'Ten ants can carries a leaf.'
items.answer: Ten ants can carry a leaf.
acceptable: it should be carry, not carries
hints: Look at the word after 'can'.
After 'can' we use the plain word.

Ten ants can carry a leaf. After 'can', the word stays plain.

items.prompt_en: Complete with 'can' or 'can't': 'One raindrop ___ fill a pot.'
items.prompt_hi: 'can' ya 'can't' lagao: 'One raindrop ___ fill a pot.' Ek boond se matka bharega kya?
items.answer: can't

items.prompt_en: The poem says, 'Together we can open doors.' Is it only about real doors? What does it mean?
items.prompt_hi: Poem kehti hai, 'Together we can open doors.' Kya sirf ghar ke darwaze ki baat hai? Iska matlab kya hai?

hints: Does a team need to open a real door?
A door can be a way into something new.
Together we can do ... things.
It means together we can find new chances and do things we cannot do alone.

items.prompt_en: Say one thing you and your friends can do together. Start with 'Together we can ...'
items.prompt_hi: Ek kaam batao jo tum aur tumhare dost saath milkar kar sakte ho. 'Together we can ...' se shuru karo.
items.answer: Any correct sentence of the form 'Together we can + plain verb', for example: Together we can clean the park.
acceptable: Together we can build a sandcastle.
Together we can win the match.
hints: Think of a big job in school or at home.
Which word comes after 'can'?
Together we can + an action word, like 'clean'.
For example: Together we can clean the park.

diagnostic.prompt_en: Meena heard the bell. Then ___ ran to the grove. 'he' or 'she'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Meena ne ghanti suni. Phir ___ grove ki taraf bhaagi. 'he' bolenge ya 'she'? Hindi mein dono ke liye 'woh' hota hai, par English mein alag hai.

items.prompt_en: Put these in order: (a) They found Gauri in the bushes. (b) Gauri did not come home. (c) Meena heard a tinkle. Which comes first?

Before searching, something went wrong.
The cow did not ...

items.prompt_en: Who heard the bell first?
items.prompt_hi: Sabse pehle ghanti ki awaaz kisne suni?
items.answer: Meena

It was a girl. Her name starts with M.
Meena heard the bell first.

items.answer: The bell on Gauri made a sound, so they followed the sound to her
acceptable: they heard the bell and followed it
the sound told them where she was
hints: It was getting dark. Could they see well?
What could they hear?
The tinkle came from the mango ...
They heard Gauri's bell and followed the sound to find her.

items.prompt_en: What do you think would happen if Gauri had no bell?

items.answer: The children might not find her in the dark
acceptable: it would be hard to find her
hints: How did they find her?
Without the bell, would there be a sound?
In the dark they could not ...
Without the bell, it would be very hard to find her in the dark.

items.prompt_en: How do you think Gopu felt when Gauri did not come home? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Jab Gauri ghar nahi aayi, Gopu ko kaisa laga hoga? Kyun?
items.answer: Worried, because Gauri was lost and it was getting dark

hints: Gopu loved the cows. One was missing.
How do you feel when you lose something you love?
He felt w-___.

items.prompt_en: 'Tinkle' and 'twinkle' sound alike. Which one is a sound, and which one is a light?
items.prompt_hi: 'Tinkle' aur 'twinkle' milte-julte hain. Kaunsa awaaz hai aur kaunsa roshni?

hints: What does a bell do? What does a star do?

A bell ... and a star ...

items.prompt_en: What is a 'grove'? Tap the picture: (a) a group of trees (b) a river (c) a house.

Mangoes grow on trees.
A mango grove has many mango ...

items.prompt_en: Gauri was stuck in 'thorny' bushes. What are thorny bushes like?

Thorny bushes have sharp thorns that prick.

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 'The friends finded Gauri in the bushes.'
items.prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 'The friends finded Gauri in the bushes.'
items.answer: The friends found Gauri in the bushes.

Some words do not take -ed.
find becomes f-___.
The friends found Gauri. 'find' becomes 'found'.

items.prompt_en: Say it in the past: 'The friends run towards the sound.' Yesterday the friends ___ towards the sound.

items.answer: ran

hints: It happened yesterday.
run does not become 'runned'.
Ran. The friends ran towards the sound.

items.prompt_en: Where did the friends find Gauri?
items.prompt_hi: Doston ko Gauri kahan mili?
items.answer: In thorny bushes in the mango grove
hints: Where did the tinkle come from?
She was stuck in something with thorns.
Near the mango trees, stuck in something with thorns ...
They found her stuck in thorny bushes in the mango grove.

items.prompt_en: Arif says: 'Meena heard the bell, and then he ran to the grove.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Arif kehta hai: 'Meena heard the bell, and then he ran to the grove.' Isme kya galat hai?
items.answer: Meena is a girl, so it should be 'she ran', not 'he ran'
acceptable: then she ran to the grove
hints: Who ran? Look at the name.
Is Meena a boy or a girl?
For a girl we say s-___.
It should be 'she ran', because Meena is a girl.

items.prompt_en: Tell the story to your little cousin in four short sentences, using 'first, next, then, at last'.

items.answer: First Gauri did not come home; next the friends went to look for her; then Meena heard the bell; at last they found Gauri and brought her home
acceptable: the cow was lost, they searched, heard the bell, found her
first Gauri was lost, at last they brought her home

What did the friends do about it?

items.prompt_en: Grandfather says the bells 'helped you find a friend'. Which part of the story did you like best, and why?

items.answer: Any part with a reason, in the form 'I liked ... because ...', for example: I liked when Meena heard the bell because it was exciting.
acceptable: I liked the end because Gauri came home.
I liked the friends because they helped each other.
hints: Think of the happiest or most exciting part.
Why did you like it?
Say: 'I liked ... because ...'
For example: I liked the end because the friends brought Gauri home safely.

steps: Find the problem at the start: Gauri did not come home.

topics.passage: Gopu lived in a small village near a river. His grandfather's cows wore little bells, and Gopu loved their tinkling sound. One evening, the cow Gauri did not come home. Gopu and his friends Meena and Arif went to look for her. It was getting dark. Suddenly Meena said, 'Shh! Listen!' From the mango grove came a soft tinkle, tinkle. The friends ran towards the sound and found Gauri stuck in some thorny bushes. Together they freed her and walked her home. Grandfather smiled. 'Those bells are not just music,' he said. 'Today they helped you find a friend.'

topics.passage: In a village in Mokokchung, Nagaland, Grandma Imna told the children an old tale. Long ago, people and tigers argued about who was stronger. 'From that tale comes our game, Hekko,' she said. The children made two teams: the Aami, who were the people, and the Aakho, who were the tigers. items.answer: A loom is the machine; a weaver is the person who weaves cloth on it

The loom is the ...; the weaver is the ...
A loom is the wooden machine; a weaver is the person who makes cloth on it.

items.answer: No; the word 'river' shows it means the land along the side of the river

Is there money near a river?

Voice goes ... at the end.

items.answer: Who lived in the fort?

For a person we use a different question word.
W-h-___ lived in the fort?
Who lived in the fort? 'Who' is for people.

items.prompt_en: Find the mistake: 'Why you came to Maheshwar?'
items.prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 'Why you came to Maheshwar?'
items.answer: Why did you come to Maheshwar?

The helper is 'did'.
Why did you ___ (came becomes ...)?
Why did you come to Maheshwar? With 'did', came becomes come.

items.prompt_en: You meet a weaver in Maheshwar. Ask her two questions with two different question words.
items.prompt_hi: Maheshwar mein tumhe ek weaver milti hain. Unse do alag question words se do sawaal poocho.
items.answer: Two correct questions, for example: How do you make a saree? How long does it take? / Who taught you?
acceptable: How long does one saree take?
Where do you sell the sarees?
hints: What would you like to know about her work?
Use Who, What, Where, When, How or Why.
Who taught ...? How long ...?
For example: Who taught you to weave? How long does one saree take?

items.prompt_en: The guide says, 'Let's go!' after Sahil's question. What will they do next?
items.prompt_hi: Sahil ke sawaal ke baad guide kehte hain, 'Let's go!' Ab woh kya karenge?
items.answer: Take a boat ride on the Narmada
acceptable: go on the river in a boat
hints: What did Sahil ask just before?
He asked about something on the river.
They will take a b-___ ride.
They will take a boat ride on the Narmada.

items.prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar mein ek mehmaan aata hai. Use kisi ek khaas jagah ke baare mein teen sentences mein batao.
items.answer: Three sentences naming the place, what is there and why it is special, for example: This is the old temple. It has a big bell. People come here on festivals.

(The ghats of Maheshwar. The river Narmada flows below.)
GUIDE: Welcome to Maheshwar, on the bank of the river Narmada.
RIYA: Look at those wide steps going into the water! What are they called?
GUIDE: They are ghats. People come here to bathe and pray.
SAHIL: Who lived in that big fort?
GUIDE: Queen Ahilyabai Holkar lived and ruled here more than two hundred years ago. She built many temples and ghats.
RIYA: (pointing) What is that wooden machine?
GUIDE: It is a loom. Weavers make the famous Maheshwari sarees on it.
SAHIL: (touching a saree gently) It is so soft! Can we take a boat ride?
